text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- British Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett says sanctions against Iraq will not be lifted until all Iraqi mass destruction weapons are removed. The United Nations imposed a trade embargo against Iraq at the start of its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
- Baghdad newspapers say the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait is the greatest event in the history of mankind.
- Parliamentarians propose a bill that would increase salaries of teachers at the state-run Kuwait University.
- Bahrain's non-oil exports to Kuwait fell to 9.1 million dinars ($29.8 million) in the first half of 1997 compared to 9.4 million in the same period of 1996.

- MP expects parliament to debate in October a government bill obliging Kuwait's foreign residents to pay health insurance fees. Currently the state imposes only nominal fees on some health care services for its 1.25 million expatriate residents.
- Police arrests seven Iranians for illegal entery.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange's index rose 5.2 points to 2,366.8 in easy trade on Saturday.
- Kuwaiti Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi to visit Tunisia.
